recommendation: Confirm Q1, Q8, G3-G18, G3-HOSTILE, and G21-NT6. Claude did adopt the round-1 G21-SCHEMA five-and-two amendment, but do not adopt its new symmetric witness-form guard or its fixed five-member schema-trigger classification. Leave all seven body-bearing CC-5 injections parked on OQ-G21-4's fixture-form/body-construction ruling: truncated bodies and invalid UTF-8 are unconditionally not schema-blocked, while duplicate members, unknown members, floats, negative integers, and over-uint53 integers remain contingent on whether OQ-G21-4 permits an envelope-level parse-failure witness with a quoted type and an unvalidated body object. A later ruling that requires an otherwise-conforming per-type body would give those five a schema dependency; that requirement is not already in the live bytes.
rationale: Independent remeasurement dated 2026-08-30 at HEAD f3b05e33479652ede37f0502084b50b590f630f7 confirmed the packet's file-08, COORD, and G-owner-residuals pins and confirmed that Claude actually moved invalid UTF-8 beside truncated bodies in r2 sections 0 and 1.1. The adoption claim is therefore true. The added guard is not: control-protocol-contract.v2.json#$.controlFrameEncoding.encoding defines the entire frame body as one UTF-8 JSON text, so raw invalid UTF-8 anywhere in the byte sequence makes the entire text invalid; there is no UTF-8-valid envelope containing a nested invalid-UTF-8 byte fragment. If bytes are escaped so the envelope remains valid UTF-8, they are not item 30. Likewise, item 29 is complete when fewer than N body bytes are delivered; a fixture author's optional choice to derive the delivered prefix from a per-type body does not make the member intrinsically schema-dependent. The general D-293 no-invention constraint already governs either witness and does not need a new member-level guard. Claude's section 1.2 discriminator also answers an open question rather than reading a rule. Items 31-35 are all parse-level violations under control-protocol-contract.v2.json#$.controlFrameEncoding.encoding and each has an envelope-level form: duplicate or unknown envelope members, or a float, negative integer, or over-uint53 integer in an envelope numeric member. Per-type dispatch need not occur. The bytes do not require each witness to be otherwise conforming except for one defect; D-293 adopted coverage rather than one-case-per-member, and the recorded rejection of non-object top level was a CC-5-membership failure because that mutation is absent from the closed CC-5 intent, not a general single-defect rule. D1-plan/G21.md#OQ-G21-4 expressly leaves unsettled whether a body may be constructed with a quoted vocabulary token without authoring that type's body schema. Therefore the five parsed-object members are contingent on OQ-G21-4, not proved exclusively schema-blocked. g21-fixture-corpus.v14.json#$.proposedLaterWork[3] is counter-evidence because it blanket-parks remaining body injections on a schema, but that pre-D-314 summary supplies no discriminator, D-314 already departed from it for truncated bodies, and OQ-G21-4 remains the governing recorded uncertainty. The five held ids have no knock-on: anti-lockstep-hostile-goldens.v3.json#$.classCoverage["CC-5"].doesNotAuthorG21RemainingCc5Injections preserves the G3-HOSTILE custody boundary and its seven-class remainder; Q1, Q8, and G3-G18 are on unrelated artifacts; and g21-leftover-join.v13.json keeps NT-6 in remainingNotAuthored.dr133 separately from remainingCc5Injections.
refutations: Claude's section 1.4 invalid-UTF-8 alternative is impossible on the governing encoding. A byte sequence containing an invalid UTF-8 fragment is not a UTF-8-valid JSON text at any nesting depth, so item 30 can never become a conforming frame body object and can never re-acquire a per-type-schema dependency.

The symmetric guard turns an optional fixture-design choice into a member-level dependency. Item 29 requires only fewer than N delivered body bytes, and item 30 requires only body bytes that are not a valid UTF-8 JSON text. Neither definition requires construction of a per-type body; D-293's existing no-invention rule is sufficient.

Claude's section 1.2 authoring test is not a recorded acceptance rule. The five parse-level defects can be placed in envelope members and rejected before per-type dispatch, while OQ-G21-4 expressly says it is unsettled whether the remaining body object may be carried with a quoted type absent a per-type schema.

The non-object-top-level rejection does not establish Claude's otherwise-conforming-except-one-defect premise. That payload failed because non-object top level is absent from the closed CC-5 intent; duplicate members, unknown members, floats, negative integers, and over-uint53 integers are each present in that intent by name.
Accordingly, Claude adopted Codex's five-and-two text but then added an unsupported condition and an unsupported fixed trigger partition. Textual adoption is not full substantive agreement.
amendments: Delete the section 1.4 symmetric guard, including the impossible nested-invalid-UTF-8 form and the claim that either raw framing member can make both triggers apply to the member.

Replace the fixed five-schema/two-raw trigger partition with two definite schema-independent members plus five OQ-G21-4-contingent members. Keep all seven named-open and author none in this recommendation.

For the five parsed-object defects, state the two lawful later routes without choosing between them now: OQ-G21-4 may permit a quoted-type envelope whose body is not validated because parse-level RF-2 fires first, or a later per-type-schema successor may provide an otherwise-conforming base.
Retain every other D-314 disposition and Claude's no-knock-on custody observation.

Leave all seven body-bearing CC-5 injections named-open on OQ-G21-4. Treat truncated bodies and invalid UTF-8 as unconditionally schema-independent. Treat duplicate members, unknown members, floats, negative integers, and over-uint53 integers as contingent: each has an envelope-level parse-failure form that does not reach per-type dispatch, but OQ-G21-4 has not decided whether its otherwise-unvalidated body object may be constructed from a quoted type without a per-type schema. refutations: Section 1.4's proposed UTF-8-valid envelope with a nested invalid-UTF-8 fragment cannot exist under control-protocol-contract.v2.json#$.controlFrameEncoding.encoding. Invalid octets anywhere make the whole frame body not a valid UTF-8 JSON text; escaped bytes remain valid UTF-8 and do not instantiate item 30.

A truncated frame never yields the exactly N-byte frame body required by transportAndFraming.framing.frame. Whether its delivered prefix happens to resemble or derive from a per-type body is a witness choice, not a schema dependency of the truncated-bodies member.

The section 1.2 test assumes a clean, otherwise-conforming frame body object, but no governing byte imposes that single-defect test. The five named parse defects can occur at envelope level and are rejected by the parse-level rule before per-type dispatch.

OQ-G21-4 itself leaves the decisive body-construction question unsettled for all seven. Filing the five parsed-object members directly on a mandatory schema trigger silently answers that open question instead of preserving it.
amendments: Remove the symmetric section 1.4 guard from both raw framing members.
Keep truncated bodies and invalid UTF-8 definitively off the schema trigger.

Move the other five from an unconditional schema trigger to OQ-G21-4's unresolved body-construction trigger; let a later owner ruling decide whether they may use an unvalidated body object or must await a per-type-schema successor.
